comments.raw_comment: A major difference that stood out to me when I analyzed these graphs was how older first time mothers increased from 1980 to 2016. Another important point is that many more women in this current time period attend college and spend most of their 20's trying to become stable in a career path than in the 1980's. College is a big expense and one that can not be payed off while simultaneously paying to raise a child. It is unrealistic to expect to be able to pay off college loans and have a child at the same time, because both are very costly. Something else that could be a reason for first time mothers becoming older is the fact that birth control and emergency contraceptives have become more accessible to women. 1980 is not many years after Roe v. Wade, so the concept of abortions and birth control was new, unknown, and not very accessible.
